title: Ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful
hookLine: the Most Merciful, whose mercy covers everything that exists

lines: I DON'T KNOW WHAT AR-RAHMAN IS.
cards: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions are camped at Hudaybiyyah, outside Mecca, and a peace treaty is being written with the Quraysh, the people who drove them out. Ali holds the pen.
The Prophet dictates the first words: bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim. And the Meccan envoy, Suhayl, stops him. As for ar-Rahman, he says, by God, I don't know what that is.
Write in Your name, O Allah, the way you used to. The companions bristle. It's the first line of the treaty, and it's already a fight.
What happens next says something about the name itself.

teach.b: The Prophet said: write it as he asks. Bismika Allahumma. In Your name, O Allah.
Bukhari records it. The name of mercy gave way so that peace could be written, and some readers see mercy itself in that. Why didn't Suhayl know the name?
The report doesn't say, but the Qur'an records Meccans asking the same thing: and what is ar-Rahman?

It comes from r-h-m, the root of mercy, and its form, fa'lan, is one that grammarians say Arabic uses for things that are full, overflowing, at their peak, like ghadban, full of anger, or 'atshan, full of thirst.
So ar-Rahman is mercy at its fullest. Scholars say the name belongs to Allah alone; no person is to be called ar-Rahman. And the Qur'an gives it an entire surah.
Surah ar-Rahman opens with the name alone, then lists gifts: the Qur'an taught, speech, the sun and moon in their courses, fruit, the palm with its sheaths, grain, the two seas.
Thirty-one times it asks, which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?
In Surah al-A'raf, in Pickthall's translation: and My mercy embraceth all things.

One classical explanation reads ar-Rahman as mercy that reaches every creature in this world, whoever they are, whatever they believe: the rain falls on every field. The name's closer partner comes tomorrow.

how: Muslims say ar-Rahman in every bismillah, and Surah ar-Rahman, with its refrain about the favors of the Lord, is often recited; Abdul-Rahman, servant of the Most Merciful, is a common name.

o: a title any very kind person can be given
mercy at its fullest, reaching all that exists
the one who judges each soul on the last day

games.q: what's inside the name — tap the pairs.
p: which of the favors will you deny?

s: people are sometimes called ar-Rahman as a title
scholars say the name belongs to Allah alone.
the Meccans at first asked what ar-Rahman was
the Qur'an records the question, and Suhayl said it at Hudaybiyyah.
the refrain of Surah ar-Rahman appears only three times
thirty-one times: which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?

games.q: the treaty's first line is disputed: the envoy won't accept ar-Rahman. you're the Prophet. what do you do?
o: have it written: in Your name, O Allah
games.why: he told Ali to write bismika Allahumma (Bukhari). the name of mercy gave way so peace could be written.

practice: With your eyes softly open, look for mercy for one minute, not the dramatic kind: the light through a window, the chair holding you up, the air arriving in your lungs without being asked, your heart doing its work while you weren't paying attention.
Name each one silently as you find it, then close your eyes and let the list keep going on its own. If you pray, you can say, ya Rahman, softly, at the end.

wordCard.voice: Ar-Rahman. The Most Merciful, mercy at its fullest, overflowing onto everything that exists, a name used only for Allah. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Most Merciful, mercy at its fullest; from r-h-m.

carryVoice: Your line: mercy covers all. Like the rain, it falls on every field, even the ones you'd pass by. That's day two hundred thirty-five.

sources.q: and My mercy embraceth all things,

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (the treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the basmala)
